visual_blueprint.sub: The fatal flaw in linear attention

motif_params.title: THE MEMORY BOTTLENECK
motif_params.sub: The fatal flaw in linear attention

beats.text: The villain is the coupling of computation and storage. It is like a librarian trying to memorize every book while reading one.
beats.visual_focus: Split screen: A librarian overwhelmed by books vs. a neural network state collapsing.

beats.text: NoteBank shatters this by decoupling storage. It archives text sparsely, replaying evidence through the model's own native forward computation.
beats.visual_focus: A sparse index table being populated alongside a neural forward pass.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—straight to the point about why linear models suck. I actually liked the librarian analogy in Beat 2; it wasn't patronizing, just a quick way to visualize the bottleneck. I got lost for a second in Beat 3 because 'replaying evidence' sounds a bit abstract, but the rest of the technical breakdown kept me interested. It didn't feel like corporate fluff, which is a huge plus.
